name: St. Wolfgang's Oak (Wolfgangseiche)

location.address: Forest path about 300 m east of Schloss Haus, Neueglofsheim, 93107 Thalmassing
location.neighbourhood: Neueglofsheim (Thalmassing), about 15 km south-east of Regensburg

official_register.name: Bavarian LfU Naturdenkmal register ND-02671 (Landkreis Regensburg ND no. 46); Nationalerbe-Baum no. 48

access: Free, open at any time. Stands on a meadow beside a field and forest path at the end of an access road with a car park; locally signposted as the landmark of Thalmassing.
transport: About 15 km from Regensburg, so a trip rather than a walk. RVV bus line 20 from Regensburg Hbf to Neueglofsheim reportedly runs on weekdays only (Moovit; not checked against a current timetable, check RVV/VGN). Then about 300 m on foot east of Schloss Haus. By car there is a car park at the end of the access road.

photo_candidate.note: Commons geotag 48.90176667, 12.182605 sits on the trunk; dated 2016-02-21 (bare). Look at the pixels before approving.

verify_notes: Pin: Nationalerbe-Baeume page GPS N48.901827 E12.182629 (measured on site) agrees within about 10 m with Rainer Lippert's 48.901768, 12.182746 and the Commons geotag 48.90176667, 12.182605; one individual crown, confirmed. Alive: baumkunde register says vital, last visit 22.08.2024; Nationalerbe-Baeume measured it Jan 2025 and designated it 21 June 2025 (lifecheck says OLD only because the Commons photo is 2016). Girth: 9.80 m (Nationalerbe-Baeume, Jan 2025 at 1.3 m; Lippert 9.80 m in 2021, 9.03 m at the waist). Earlier: 8 m in 1905 (at 1 m), 8.40 m in 1990 (Froehlich). The trunk is buttressed with huge knobs and root flare, so girth depends on measuring height; NEB says the waist sits near 2 m. Height about 18 m (Lippert 2021), about 20 m (NEB). Age: sources disagree widely: about 500 (Lippert), up to 600 (baumkunde), 700 to 850 (NEB, about 800); a legend says 1250 years; NEB notes mentions range from 400 to 1300 years. Kept broad, legend not a basis. Sources: state ND register plus the Nationalerbe-Baeume initiative plus Lippert's own measurements. Story facts: legend says St. Wolfgang preached from the great horizontal limb; that limb, over 10 m long, has rested on three props for over a century (visible on old drawings and photos, 1905 photograph by Friedrich Stuetzer); the oak burned in 1878 and in 1909, the latter on St. Wolfgang's day; lightning struck it repeatedly; oval opening in the trunk from an ancient limb break; hollow trunk; restored in 1972 by Landkreis Regensburg and Gemeinde Thalmassing. One of the largest oaks in Bavaria. Stand-alone, 15 km out: belongs to Thalmassing/Neueglofsheim and may suit a tree page of its own rather than the Regensburg walk.
